children: has asked Brazil's power regulator Aneel to annul proceedings aimed at terminating its Sao Paulo distribution concession, saying the regulator failed to conduct a structured analysis of the impact on consumers.
Aneel described the filing submitted on Thursday as Enel's final defense before the regulator decides whether to recommend termination of the concession to the federal government.

Aneel had previously concluded that Enel's Sao Paulo distributor has "structural failures," citing poor performance during extreme weather events in 2023, 2024 and 2025, when millions of consumers were hit by prolonged power outages.
Enel said it complied with the two official service-quality indicators that could underpin a termination recommendation.
It said the December 2025 event was "unprecedented and extraordinary" and that Aneel was disregarding performance improvements since 2023.
Enel also renewed a request for an independent technical audit that the regulator denied in August after criticism from Aneel board members.
Brazil's Mines and Energy Ministry has the final say on whether to terminate the concession and may follow or disregard Aneel's recommendation.
